et ur.explanation: "Et ur" means "a clock / watch". To say a watch you wear on your wrist, use "et armbåndsur" (a wristwatch): "Jeg har et armbåndsur på" (I am wearing a wristwatch). Do not mix it up with "klokken" (o'clock), which is used for telling the time: "Hvad er klokken?" (What time is it?)

uacceptabel.explanation: "Uacceptabel" means "unacceptable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "acceptabel" (acceptable). To say a result is not good enough, use it before the noun: "et uacceptabelt resultat" (an unacceptable result).

uafgjort.explanation: "Uafgjort" means "tied", as in a game where both sides have the same score. It is built from "u-" (not) and "afgjort" (decided), so literally it is undecided.

uafhængig.explanation: "Uafhængig" means "independent". It is built from "u-" (not) and "afhængig" (dependent). To say who you are independent of, add "af" (of): "Hun er uafhængig af sine forældre" (She is independent of her parents).

uafhængighed.explanation: "Uafhængighed" means "independence". It is built from "uafhængig" (independent) and the ending "-hed". To describe a person, use "uafhængig" instead: "Hun er uafhængig" (She is independent).

uanset.explanation: "Uanset" means "no matter". Before a noun it means "regardless of": "uanset alder" (regardless of age). Before a question word it means "no matter what": "uanset hvad" (no matter what).

uanstændig.explanation: "Uanstændig" means "indecent". It is built from "u-" (not) and "anstændig" (decent). For a different use, say prices are far too high: "uanstændigt høje priser" (indecently high prices).

uansvarlig.explanation: "Uansvarlig" means "irresponsible". It is built from "u-" (not) and "ansvarlig" (responsible). To call an action irresponsible, use it after "det er" (it is): "Det er uansvarligt at køre så hurtigt" (It is irresponsible to drive that fast).

uartig.explanation: "Uartig" means "naughty". It is built from "u-" (not) and "artig" (well-behaved). To tell a child they have been naughty: "Du har været uartig" (You have been naughty).

ubegribelig.explanation: "Ubegribelig" means "incomprehensible". It is built from "u-" (not), "at begribe" (to grasp) and "-elig" (can be), so literally it cannot be grasped. To say something makes no sense to you: "Det er mig ubegribeligt" (I cannot understand it).

ubehagelig.explanation: "Ubehagelig" means "unpleasant". It is built from "u-" (not) and "behagelig" (pleasant). To describe a person you do not like being around: "en ubehagelig person" (an unpleasant person). To say a situation feels awkward, it also means "uncomfortable": "Det er ubehageligt" (It is uncomfortable).

ubekymret.explanation: "Ubekymret" means "carefree". It is built from "u-" (not) and "bekymret" (worried). To describe a childhood without worries: "en ubekymret barndom" (a carefree childhood).

ubelejlig.explanation: "Ubelejlig" means "inconvenient". It is built from "u-" (not) and "belejlig" (convenient). To ask whether you are interrupting someone, say: "Kommer jeg ubelejligt?" (Is this a bad time?)

ubestemt.explanation: "Ubestemt" means "vague". It is built from "u-" (not) and "bestemt" (specific). To describe a feeling you cannot name: "en ubestemt følelse" (a vague feeling). To say something has no end date, use "på ubestemt tid" (for an unspecified time).

ubestemt form.explanation: "Ubestemt form" means "indefinite form". To put a noun in this form, say it with "en" or "et" before it: "en bil" (a car), "et hus" (a house). The form with "the" adds an ending: "bilen" (the car).

ubetydelig.explanation: "Ubetydelig" means "insignificant". It is built from "u-" (not) and "betydelig" (significant). To say damage is too small to matter: "Skaden er ubetydelig" (The damage is insignificant).

ubevæbnet.explanation: "Ubevæbnet" means "unarmed". It is built from "u-" (not) and "bevæbnet" (armed). To describe a guard with no weapon: "en ubevæbnet vagt" (an unarmed guard).

ubrugelig.explanation: "Ubrugelig" means "useless". The opposite is "brugbar" (usable). To say what something is useless for, add "til" (for): "Den er ubrugelig til dette" (It is useless for this).

ud over.explanation: "Ud over" means "besides". To add one more thing to what you already named: "Ud over kaffe har vi te" (Besides coffee, we have tea). It is built from "ud" (out) and "over" (over). The spelling "udover" also exists.

ud over det.explanation: "Ud over det" means "besides that". To add one more point to what you just said: "Ud over det er det for dyrt" (Besides that, it is too expensive). It is built from "ud over" (besides) and "det" (that).

udadvendt.explanation: "Udadvendt" means "outgoing". Literally it means "turned outward". The opposite is "indadvendt" (withdrawn, quiet), literally "turned inward": "Han er indadvendt og siger ikke meget" (He is withdrawn and does not say much).

uddannet.explanation: "Uddannet" means "qualified", as in having finished the training for a job. To say which job, say it right after: "Hun er uddannet tømrer" (She is a trained carpenter). It also means "educated": "Hun er højt uddannet" (She is highly educated).

ude af øje, ude af sind.explanation: "Ude af øje, ude af sind" means "out of sight, out of mind". Literally, it is "out of eye, out of mind". "Ude af" means "out of" in other phrases too: "ude af kontrol" (out of control).

udefra.explanation: "Udefra" means "from outside". It is built from "ude" (outside) and "fra" (from). To say you look at something as an outsider: "Set udefra ser det nemt ud" (Seen from outside, it looks easy).

udelukkende.explanation: "Udelukkende" means "only". It comes from the verb "at udelukke" (to exclude), so it means everything else is left out. To say a shop sells one kind of food and nothing else: "Butikken sælger udelukkende økologisk mad" (The shop sells only organic food).

udelukket.explanation: "Udelukket" means "excluded". It comes from the verb "at udelukke" (to exclude). To say something cannot happen, use "Det er udelukket" (It is out of the question) as a firm answer to a suggestion.

uden tvivl.explanation: "Uden tvivl" means "without a doubt". It is built from "uden" (without) and "tvivl" (doubt). To agree strongly with a question: "Er det en god idé?" "Uden tvivl!" (Is it a good idea? Without a doubt!)

udenad.explanation: "Udenad" means "by heart". To say you learn something by heart, use "at lære noget udenad" (to learn something by heart).

udenfor.explanation: "Udenfor" means "outside". To say where someone is: "Hunden sover udenfor" (The dog sleeps outside). To say where someone goes: "Vi går udenfor" (We go outside).

udenlandsk.explanation: "Udenlandsk" means "foreign". Do not mix it up with "udenlands" (abroad), which says where someone goes or is: "Hun bor udenlands" (She lives abroad).

udholdenhed.explanation: "En udholdenhed" means "endurance". It is built from "at holde ud" (to hold out, to endure) and the ending "-hed".

udkig.explanation: "Et udkig" means "lookout", as in a high place to look from. To say you are searching for something, use "på udkig efter" (on the lookout for): "Jeg er på udkig efter en lejlighed" (I am on the lookout for an apartment). Do not mix it up with "en udsigt" (a view), which is what you see: "Der er en flot udsigt" (There is a nice view).

udlændingepolitik.explanation: "En udlændingepolitik" means "an immigration policy". It is built from "udlændinge" (foreigners) and "politik" (policy), so literally it is a foreigner policy.

udmattet.explanation: "Udmattet" means "exhausted". It comes from the verb "at udmatte" (to wear out). Do not mix it up with "træt" (tired), which is milder: "Jeg er træt" (I am tired) and "Jeg er udmattet" (I am exhausted).

udmærket.explanation: "Udmærket" means "excellent". As a reply that agrees to a suggestion, it also means "fine": "Kan vi mødes klokken ti?" "Udmærket!" (Can we meet at ten? Fine!)

udover.explanation: "Udover" means "besides", adding something to what you already named. It can also mean "beyond": "udover det sædvanlige" (beyond the usual). The two-word spelling "ud over" also exists.

udsat.explanation: "Udsat" means "vulnerable", as in a group open to harm: "en udsat gruppe" (a vulnerable group). When something is open to a danger, it means "exposed", with "for" (to): "udsat for kulde" (exposed to cold). When something is moved to a later time, it means "postponed": "Mødet er udsat" (The meeting is postponed).

udsolgt.explanation: "Udsolgt" means "sold out". It is built from "ud" (out) and "solgt" (sold). To say a show has no tickets left: "Koncerten er udsolgt" (The concert is sold out).

udstyr.explanation: "Udstyr" means "equipment". This word has no article, so leave out "et": "Jeg har mit eget udstyr med" (I have my own equipment with me).

uduelig.explanation: "Uduelig" means "incompetent". It is built from "u-" (not) and "duelig" (capable), so literally it is not capable.

udødelig.explanation: "Udødelig" means "immortal". It is built from "u-" (not) and "dødelig" (mortal). To say a work will be remembered forever, use it for the work: "Shakespeares værker er udødelige" (Shakespeare's works are immortal).

uendelig.explanation: "Uendelig" means "endless". It is built from "u-" (not) and "endelig" (final). To make a feeling stronger, put it before the feeling word: "Jeg er uendelig taknemmelig" (I am endlessly grateful).

uerfaren.explanation: "Uerfaren" means "inexperienced". It is built from "u-" (not) and "erfaren" (experienced).

ufattelig.explanation: "Ufattelig" means "unthinkable". It is built from "u-" (not), "at fatte" (to grasp) and "-elig" (can be), so literally it cannot be grasped. When something is far bigger than you expected, it also means "incredible": "et ufatteligt tal" (an incredible number). To make a word stronger, put it before that word: "ufattelig smuk" (unbelievably beautiful).

uforglemmelig.explanation: "Uforglemmelig" means "unforgettable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "-elig" (can be) around the verb "at glemme" (to forget), so literally it cannot be forgotten. To describe something you lived through: "en uforglemmelig oplevelse" (an unforgettable experience).

uformel.explanation: "Uformel" means "informal". It is built from "u-" (not) and "formel" (formal). To describe clothes that are not smart: "uformelt tøj" (informal clothes).

uforskammet.explanation: "Uforskammet" means "rude". To say a price is shockingly high, put it before the price word: "uforskammet dyrt" (outrageously expensive).

uforudsigelig.explanation: "Uforudsigelig" means "unpredictable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "forudsigelig" (predictable).

ugen efter.explanation: "Ugen efter" means "the week after". To say something happened in the week after a party: "Ugen efter festen var jeg syg" (The week after the party I was sick). For the day after, use "dagen efter": "Dagen efter rejste hun" (The day after, she left).

ugevis.explanation: "Ugevis" means "for weeks". It is built from "en uge" (a week) and the ending "-vis", which gives the meaning "week after week". To say you waited a long time: "Vi ventede ugevis" (We waited for weeks).

ugift.explanation: "Ugift" means "unmarried". It is built from "u-" (not) and "gift" (married). The same "u-" is in "uvenlig" (unfriendly), the opposite of "venlig" (friendly).

ugyldig.explanation: "Ugyldig" means "invalid". It is built from "u-" (not) and "gyldig" (valid). To say a code cannot be used: "Koden er ugyldig" (The code is invalid).

uheldig.explanation: "Uheldig" means "unlucky". It is built from "u-" (not) and "heldig" (lucky). When something turns out badly, it means "unfortunate": "en uheldig bemærkning" (an unfortunate remark).

uhyggelig.explanation: "Uhyggelig" means "creepy". It is built from "u-" (not) and "hyggelig" (cozy). To say a place gives you the creeps: "Huset er uhyggeligt" (The house is creepy).

uhyre.explanation: "Uhyre" means "immensely". To make an adjective stronger, put it before the adjective: "uhyre vigtig" (immensely important). As a noun, it takes "et" and means a monster: "et uhyre" (a monster).

uhøflig.explanation: "Uhøflig" means "rude". It is built from "u-" (not) and "høflig" (polite). To say who someone is rude to, add "mod" (to): "Vær ikke uhøflig mod din lærer" (Do not be rude to your teacher).

ukendt.explanation: "Ukendt" means "unknown". It is built from "u-" (not) and "kendt" (known). To say you do not know someone: "Han er ukendt for mig" (He is unknown to me).

ukraine.explanation: "Ukraine" means "Ukraine". To say where you are, use "i" (in): "Jeg bor i Ukraine" (I live in Ukraine). To say where you go, use "til" (to): "Vi rejser til Ukraine" (We travel to Ukraine).

ukrainsk.explanation: "Ukrainsk" means "Ukrainian". It is built from "Ukraine" (Ukraine) and the ending "-sk". English writes "Ukrainian" starting with U, but Danish writes "ukrainsk" starting with u.

ukrudt.explanation: "Ukrudt" means "weeds". This word has no article, so leave out "et": "Der er meget ukrudt i haven" (There are a lot of weeds in the garden).

uld.explanation: "Uld" means "wool". This word has no article. To say what something is made of, use "af" (of): "Sokkerne er af uld" (The socks are made of wool).

ulige.explanation: "Ulige" means "odd", as in an odd number such as 3 or 7. It is built from "u-" (not) and "lige" (even). For a different use, it means "unequal": "en ulige kamp" (an unequal fight).

ulovlig.explanation: "Ulovlig" means "illegal". It is built from "u-" (not) and "lovlig" (legal). To say the law forbids something: "Det er ulovligt at parkere her" (It is illegal to park here).

ultimativ.explanation: "Ultimativ" means "ultimate", as in the best or most extreme of its kind. It also means "final", as in a demand that leaves no room to negotiate: "et ultimativt krav" (a final demand).

ulydig.explanation: "Ulydig" means "disobedient". It is built from "u-" (not) and "lydig" (obedient).

ulykkelig.explanation: "Ulykkelig" means "unhappy". It is built from "u-" (not) and "lykkelig" (happy). To say someone is unhappy because of an event: "Han er ulykkelig efter bruddet" (He is unhappy after the breakup).

ulækker.explanation: "Ulækker" means "disgusting". Its opposite is "lækker" (tasty, nice): "Kagen er lækker" (The cake is tasty).

umiddelbart.explanation: "Umiddelbart" means "at first sight", before you look closer. When you put it in front of "efter" (after), it means "right": "umiddelbart efter mødet" (right after the meeting).

umoden.explanation: "Umoden" means "immature". It is built from "u-" (not) and "moden" (ripe, grown-up). For fruit that is not ready to eat, it means "unripe": "et umodent æble" (an unripe apple).

umulig.explanation: "Umulig" means "impossible". It is built from "u-" (not) and "mulig" (possible). When you say a person is hard to deal with, it also means "impossible" in that sense: "Du er umulig!" (You are impossible!)

under.explanation: "Under" means "under". To say where something is, use it before a place: "Katten sover under sengen" (The cat sleeps under the bed). To say when something happens, it means "during": "under ferien" (during the holiday). Before a number, it means "less than": "under ti" (under ten).

under alle omstændigheder.explanation: "Under alle omstændigheder" means "in any case". It is built from "under" (under), "alle" (all) and "omstændigheder" (circumstances), so literally it is under all circumstances. To say something must never happen, use "under ingen omstændigheder" (under no circumstances): "Det må under ingen omstændigheder ske" (It must not happen under any circumstances).

underbukser.explanation: "Underbukser" means "underpants". It is built from "under" (under) and "bukser" (pants). To say one item, use "et par" (a pair of): "et par underbukser" (a pair of underpants).

underholdende.explanation: "Underholdende" means "entertaining". It comes from the verb "at underholde" (to entertain). To say how a show was: "Showet var meget underholdende" (The show was very entertaining).

underholdning.explanation: "En underholdning" means "entertainment". It comes from the verb "at underholde" (to entertain). To say a place offers it for free: "Der er gratis underholdning" (There is free entertainment).

underlig.explanation: "Underlig" means "weird". To say you find something odd: "Det er underligt, at han ikke ringer" (It is weird that he does not call).

undertøj.explanation: "Undertøj" means "underwear". It is built from "under" (under) and "tøj" (clothes). This word has no article, so leave out "et": "Jeg har købt nyt undertøj" (I bought new underwear).

undervejs.explanation: "Undervejs" means "along the way". To say something has not arrived yet: "Pakken er undervejs" (The package is on its way). To say where you are heading, use "på vej" (on the way) with "til" (to): "på vej til skolen" (on the way to school).

undervisning.explanation: "Undervisning" means "teaching", as in lessons at a school. To say when the lessons start: "Undervisningen begynder klokken otte" (Classes begin at eight).

undskyld.explanation: "Undskyld" means "sorry / excuse me". To apologize: "Undskyld, jeg kom for sent" (Sorry, I came too late). To get someone's attention politely: "Undskyld, må jeg komme forbi?" (Excuse me, may I get past?). To ask someone to repeat because you did not hear, say "Undskyld?" (Pardon?)

undskyld mig.explanation: "Undskyld mig" means "excuse me". It is built from "undskyld" (sorry) and "mig" (me). To get someone's attention: "Undskyld mig, hvor er stationen?" (Excuse me, where is the station?)

undtagen.explanation: "Undtagen" means "except". It comes from the verb "at undtage" (to make an exception). To say a rule has an exception: "Reglen gælder for alle undtagen børn" (The rule applies to everyone except children).

undvigende.explanation: "Undvigende" means "evasive". It comes from the verb "at undvige" (to dodge).

ung.explanation: "Ung" means "young". To talk about young people in general, say "de unge" (the young): "De unge bruger telefonen meget" (Young people use the phone a lot).

ungdom.explanation: "Ungdom" means "youth". It is built from "ung" (young) and the ending "-dom", which is also in "sygdom" (illness), from "syg" (sick).

unik.explanation: "Unik" means "unique". To say a chance is rare and special: "Det er en unik chance" (It is a unique chance).

unødvendig.explanation: "Unødvendig" means "unnecessary". It is built from "u-" (not) and "nødvendig" (necessary). To say something can be skipped: "Det er unødvendigt at betale to gange" (It is unnecessary to pay twice).

uovervindelig.explanation: "Uovervindelig" means "invincible". It is built from "u-" (not), "at overvinde" (to overcome) and "-elig" (can be), so literally it cannot be overcome. The same "-elig" is in "ubegribelig" (incomprehensible).

upassende.explanation: "Upassende" means "inappropriate". It is built from "u-" (not) and "passende" (suitable). To say clothes do not suit an event: "upassende tøj til en begravelse" (inappropriate clothes for a funeral).

upopulær.explanation: "Upopulær" means "unpopular". It is built from "u-" (not) and "populær" (popular). To say a decision upsets many people: "en upopulær beslutning" (an unpopular decision).

upraktisk.explanation: "Upraktisk" means "impractical". It is built from "u-" (not) and "praktisk" (handy). To say shoes are hard to use: "Skoene er upraktiske" (The shoes are impractical).

upålidelig.explanation: "Upålidelig" means "unreliable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "pålidelig" (dependable). To say a source cannot be trusted: "Kilden er upålidelig" (The source is unreliable).

urealistisk.explanation: "Urealistisk" means "unrealistic". It is built from "u-" (not) and "realistisk" (realistic). To say a goal can work in real life: "Det er et realistisk mål" (It is a realistic goal).

urolig.explanation: "Urolig" means "uneasy". It is built from "u-" (not) and "rolig" (calm). To say you worry about someone, add "for" (about): "Han er urolig for sin hund" (He is uneasy about his dog). It also means "restless": "en urolig nat" (a restless night).
